data.title: PR-20 IMPL-04: repair-transaction semantic and protected-intent diff computed from the stores; weakenings reclassified as privileged revisions; claimed diffs verified byte-equal

data.body: [HIGH] Program changes can silently authorize stale evidence reuse. assemble_minted always passes an empty semantic_changes list while it still passes every scoped evidence record. For an applied Rust repair that keeps the base intent, the assembler sees no changed field. compute_impact therefore leaves every record as Reused(NoDependencyOnAnyChange) at crates/continuum-semantic-diff/src/impact.rs:532-568. The artifact can report policy allow, gate 3 passed, and evidence reused although no program-side classification occurred. This contradicts the stated rule that an unrequested layer cannot prove absence. It can let pre-repair evidence survive a behavior-changing patch after evaluation wires this API. Return a typed inconclusive or unknown impact until program classification is complete. An explicit completeness marker that forbids reuse from incomplete layers is another safe design. Add a regression with an applied Rust change and nonempty pre-repair evidence. Failure modes: incomplete program classification produces false reuse; store failures already fail closed; a large complete scope can also exhaust memory before a typed outcome. Edge cases: same intent with changed Rust, same intent with nonempty evidence, rebinds with equal semantic content, duplicate evidence identities, and concurrent base supersession. Rollback: disable this adapter or return inconclusive for applied program changes until the semantic layer exists; no production caller exists in this range. Monitoring: count passed gate 3 artifacts with differing snapshots, empty semantic_changes, and nonempty reused; also track scope size and inconclusive reasons. Validation: assert that a Rust change plus scoped evidence never reaches reused without classified changes and a witnessed independence path; retain forged-claim, store-silence, duplicate-scope, and standing tests. The separate risk:critical human approval gate remains required.

data.reason: HIGH: program-side classification is omitted while scoped evidence can be emitted as reused. Resolve th-2fdcqz before approval.

data.body: Fixed per lead ruling (fail closed while no program-side classifier exists). continuum-semantic-diff gains ProgramLayer {Classified, Unclassified}, UnknownCause::ProgramLayerUnclassified, compute_impact_under and assemble_under (assemble/compute_impact unchanged = Classified). continuum_repair::diff assembles under Unclassified unless the candidate is byte-identical to its base. Under Unclassified every scoped evidence entry joins Unknown(ProgramLayerUnclassified): nothing is emitted as reused; each entry is unknown or invalidated (revalidate). A repair (intent preserved, allow) now gets gate 3 inconclusive with INV-008 reason Unsupported, never passed; so gate 3 cannot pass today for any workspace-changing candidate, stated in diff.rs docs, the START_HERE bullet and the review record; owner is the missing program-side classifier. The empty semantic_changes is typed Unclassified via DiffArtifact::program_layer. The wire schema cannot express 'not classified' (closed 7-axis kind, closed objects), so on the wire the only trace is empty semantic_changes plus an impact with nothing reused; no schema change made, raised as follow-up. Regressions: pr20_impl04_neg_13 (applied rust change + same intent, and equal-content rebinding, with pre-repair evidence incl. witnessed independence: reused==0, all revalidated; non-vacuity: identical candidate reuses both), pr20_impl04_neg_14 (empty section never read as no change: allow + Unclassified -> gate 3 inconclusive; only identical candidate passes), impact.rs::an_unclassified_program_layer_licenses_no_reuse; pos_01 now asserts inconclusive/Unsupported. Scope-size exhaustion: scope comes from the daemon store; bound left to the daemon wiring (documented).

data.body:
[HIGH][risk:high] The fail-closed program-layer fact is absent from the canonical artifact and its identity. DiffArtifact stores program here, but artifact_json omits it at crates/continuum-semantic-diff/src/artifact.rs:536-617. Gate 3 branches on this private state at crates/continuum-repair/src/diff.rs:495-502. The diff handle hashes only the rendered JSON at crates/continuum-repair/src/diff.rs:661-671. The differential test demonstrates the collision at crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr20_impl04_semantic_intent_diff.rs:345-367: the repair subject is Unclassified because its snapshots differ, the oracle uses assemble and is Classified, yet their canonical bytes are equal. With empty evidence, both also carry policy allow, empty semantic_changes, and the same diff_* identity. A persisted, cached, or cross-operation consumer cannot recover whether semantic_changes is complete. It can reinterpret an unclassified diff as classified and change gate 3 from inconclusive to passed. Add a normative wire completeness or requested-layer field. Include it in the canonical bytes and diff identity. Derive gate and impact behavior from that durable field. Keep IMPL-04 active until this is representable and reload-safe.

Failure modes: persistence drops the private marker; one diff identity denotes both pass and inconclusive; cache reuse upgrades an unclassified result.

Edge cases: empty evidence, already-invalidated evidence, identical versus changed snapshots, reload from canonical bytes, cross-site diff reuse, and classifier-version changes.

Rollback: do not wire publication, repair.evaluate, or repair.promote. Revert the delivered status or keep this slice scaffold-only until the schema moves.

Monitoring: reject changed-snapshot diffs without durable program completeness. Count any handle observed with more than one typed completeness state.

Validation: prove Classified and Unclassified produce distinct bytes and handles. Round-trip both through the wire and assert that unclassified never passes gate 3. Retain the stale-evidence tests.

The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains mandatory. This static review cannot waive it.

data.reason: BLOCK: HIGH th-1k7ib7. ProgramLayer changes gate 3 from passed to inconclusive, but canonical bytes and the diff_* identity omit it. Persisted or cached artifacts cannot preserve the fail-closed state. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

data.body: Fixed within the current contract, no schema change. (1) The layer is bound into the identity: diff::mint_handle hashes layer_tag(program) || 0x00 || canonical-bytes-without-diff_id, with versioned tags semantic-diff/program-layer/{classified,unclassified}/v1 (fixed set, no NUL, so injective). The handle is the artifact's diff_id, so the two layers never share bytes either. verify_claimed_diff and verify_claimed_handle derive the layer from the stores and, on mismatch, recompute under the other layer only to name the refusal: a claim minted under the other layer is DiffClaimRefusal::LayerMismatch{computed}. (2) diff::gate_status_of_cached is the only path from stored bytes to a gate status: it recomputes from the stores and accepts the cached bytes only if byte-equal to the recompute; a stale or other-layer cache is refused typed, and bytes whose layer cannot be established this way yield no gate status at all (stricter than defaulting to Unclassified). (3) The wire impact arrays hold bare artifact ids (pattern-only strings) with no cause token, so the schema cannot name ProgramLayerUnclassified there; left for the batched user decision. Tests: pr20_impl04_neg_15 (equal bytes under two layers -> distinct handles), neg_16 (classified handle/bytes for an unclassified recompute -> LayerMismatch; unclassified verifies), neg_17 (cached classified artifact -> refused; honest cache -> Inconclusive; garbage -> Disagrees; silent store -> Undiffable; non-vacuity: identical-candidate cache -> Passed). Retained fixtures re-blessed with the tagged handles.

[RESOLVED][risk:high] The target fix closes the identity and persistence collision. The versioned layer tag enters the diff handle preimage at crates/continuum-repair/src/diff.rs:697-725, the handle enters canonical bytes at crates/continuum-repair/src/diff.rs:734-773, and cached bytes can reach a gate status only after authoritative recomputation and byte equality at crates/continuum-repair/src/diff.rs:831-928. Failure modes: classified-cache substitution becomes LayerMismatch; forged bytes or handles are refused; silent stores remain Undiffable; unclassified changed snapshots remain inconclusive with no reuse. Edge cases: empty evidence, equal versus changed snapshots, equal-content rebinding, duplicates, garbage cache bytes, and unavailable stores have explicit coverage at crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr20_impl04_semantic_intent_diff.rs:919-1119. Rollback: do not wire repair.evaluate or repair.promote, or revert this adapter, if recomputation cannot stay authoritative. Monitoring: count LayerMismatch, Disagrees, and Undiffable outcomes; alert on any changed-snapshot Passed result; bound and track evidence-scope size in daemon wiring. Validation: static review covered the full persisted range and the dedicated regressions; no test command ran because this reviewer may write only Seal metadata. The schema still lacks an explicit completeness field, so publication must retain the recompute-only contract. That residual is not a bypass in this unwired slice. The separate risk:critical human approval gate remains mandatory.
